Usage: lexisharp benchmark <corpus-dir> --queries <file> --qrels <file> [options]
  --queries <file>    Labeled queries: a JSON object {"id": "text", ...} or a TSV 'id\ttext'
  --qrels <file>       Relevance judgments: TSV 'qid\tdocid[\tgrade]', one per line ('#' comments)
  --top-k <n>          Retrieval depth for every metric (default: 10)
  --limit <n>          Cap the number of queries evaluated (default: all)
  --configs <list>     Comma-separated: bm25, bm25-tuned, tfidf, ql, hybrid, bm25-semantic, bm25f, bm25f-title, bm25f-tuned, bm25-proximity, bm25-proximity-full, bm25-proximity-boost, bm25+, bm25+-tuned, bm25l, bm25l-tuned (default: bm25,tfidf,ql,hybrid,bm25-tuned)
  --metric <name>      Objective the *-tuned configs maximize: precision, recall, f1, ndcg (default: f1)
  --json <path>        Write the results as JSON to this file
  --help, -h           Show this help

Usage: lexisharp diff <corpus-dir> --queries <file> --qrels <file> --baseline <cfg> --candidate <cfg>
  Compares two configurations query by query: which ones the candidate rescued, which it
  lost, and where the first judged document moved. A pair of means cannot show that.
  --baseline <cfg>     The reference configuration (same names as --configs)
  --candidate <cfg>    The configuration being evaluated
  --epsilon <n>        Score difference ignored when calling a query moved (default: 1e-9)
  Other options: --queries, --qrels, --top-k, --limit

Usage: lexisharp baseline <corpus-dir> --queries <file> --qrels <file> --out <file>
  Records what every configuration returns, per query, as a reviewable diff. Writing the
  baseline is a separate command on purpose: re-recording it must be a deliberate, visible
  act and review, not a flag that quietly accepts whatever the code now does.
  --out <file>         Where to write the baseline
  Other options: --queries, --qrels, --top-k, --limit, --configs

Usage: lexisharp verify <corpus-dir> --queries <file> --qrels <file> --against <file>
  Replays the run and checks it against a recorded baseli

result.stdout:
Usage: lexisharp segment build <corpus-dir> [--store <dir>] [--analyzer <name>]
  Index the corpus into a store and commit it. The store defaults to .lexisharp in the
  current directory, which is where 'lexisharp search' looks. Analyzer: default or english.
Usage: lexisharp segment add <store-dir> --corpus <dir>
  Add the corpus's documents to the store's live overlay and commit.
Usage: lexisharp segment remove <store-dir> --id <doc-id>
  Tombstone a document and commit.
Usage: lexisharp segment commit <store-dir>
  Compact the store: merge its tombstones and rewrite one segment on disk.
Usage: lexisharp segment search <store-dir> --query <text> [--top-k <n>] [--json <path>]
  Search the committed store and print the ranked hits.
Usage: lexisharp segment info <store-dir>
  Report the store's counts without searching it.
